newsitem.title: INDIA: India to spend 83 bln rupees to develop railways.
newsitem.headline: India to spend 83 bln rupees to develop railways.

text.p: India has set aside an outlay of 83 billion rupees ($2.32 billion) as development plan expenditure in 1997/98 (April-March) for the nation's railway network, Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan said on Wednesday.

In 1996/97, the annual plan outlay was initially fixed at 81.3 billion rupees but was later modified to 83 billion rupees, he told the Indian parliament, while presenting the Railway Budget for 1997/98.
Paswan said the 1997/98 outlay will enjoy a budgetary support of 18.31 billion rupees which is four billion rupees higher than the budgetary support in 1996/97.

The railways would raise 34.19 billion rupees from their own resources and the remaining amount of 30.50 billion rupees was proposed to be raised through issue of bonds by the Indian Railway Finance Corp and private investment, he said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
